s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic bone pain with progressive worsening and multi-system involvement
salient_findings: Diffuse bone pain around the knees and elbows
Intermittent generalized pruritus
Bilateral exophthalmos and blurred vision
Mild thrombocytosis and elevated inflammatory markers
Bilateral symmetric sclerotic changes on radiographs
Multifocal intramedullary sclerosis on CT and MRI
key_facts: 36-year-old man with no prior medical history
4-year history of diffuse bone pain
Bone pain worsened over the past 2 months
Developed blurred vision, bilateral exophthalmos, and difficulty walking
Previous workups were nondiagnostic
Treated with analgesics, vitamin D, topical steroids, and antihistamines
Normal white-cell count and differential
Normal hemoglobin
Mild thrombocytosis
Normal renal and liver function tests
Negative tumor markers and autoimmune serologies
Mildly elevated C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
Bilateral symmetric sclerotic changes on knee radiographs
Intramedullary sclerosis of the distal humeri on humeral radiographs
Sclerosis of the proximal ulnae and radii on forearm radiographs
Bilateral symmetric uptake on 99mTc bone scintigraphy and FDG-PET
Multifocal intramedullary sclerosis on CT and MRI of the lower limbs
Enhancing lesions in the pituitary gland and retrobulbar soft tissues on MRI
FDG-avid lesions on PET/CT of the brain
Bilateral perinephric soft-tissue thickening with FDG uptake on CT and PET/CT of the abdomen
CT-guided biopsy of the left proximal tibia showed diffuse infiltration by foamy histiocytes and fibrosis

Tuberous sclerosis complex with bone lesions
per_call: Diaphyseal medullary stenosis with bone sclerosis
Tuberous sclerosis complex with bone lesions

shortlist.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
shortlist.why_kept: Diffuse infiltration by foamy histiocytes and fibrosis with rare Touton-like giant cells, consistent with Erdheim-Chester disease

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation, but histiocyte staining negative for CD1a, S100, and langerin, making Erdheim-Chester disease more likely

shortlist.label: Sclerosteosis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral symmetric sclerotic changes on radiographs, but absence of other characteristic features such as syndactyly

shortlist.label: Paget's disease of bone
shortlist.why_kept: Bone pain and sclerosis, but lack of characteristic laboratory and radiographic findings

shortlist.label: Chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Bone pain and sclerosis, but absence of other characteristic features such as recurrent infections

raw.rationale: The presence of diffuse infiltration by foamy histiocytes and fibrosis with rare Touton-like giant cells on biopsy, along with the involvement of multiple systems including bones, brain, and kidneys, is more consistent with Erdheim-Chester disease than Paget's disease of bone.
raw.anchor_refutation: Paget's disease of bone typically presents with an abnormal bone remodeling process leading to bone deformities and does not usually involve the brain or kidneys, nor does it typically show the specific histiocytic infiltration pattern seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Paget's disease of bone
rejected.why: Does not explain the systemic involvement or the specific histiocytic pattern on biopsy

rejected.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: Immunohistochemical staining negative for CD1a, S100, and langerin does not support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Sclerosteosis
rejected.why: Typically presents with skeletal abnormalities and does not involve the brain or kidneys

rejected.label: Chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis
rejected.why: Does not typically show the diffuse infiltration by foamy histiocytes or the specific systemic involvement seen in this patient
